The '''2020–21 season''' was the [[List of FC Barcelona seasons|122nd season]] in the existence of '''[[FC Barcelona|Futbol Club Barcelona]]''' and its 91st consecutive season in the top flight of [[Football in Spain|Spanish football]]. In addition to the [[2020–21 La Liga|domestic league]], Barcelona participated in this season's editions of the [[2020–21 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]], the [[2020–21 Supercopa de España|Supercopa de España]], and the [[2020–21 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]]. The season covered the period from 15 August 2020 to 30 June 2021, with the late start to the season due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain|COVID-19 pandemic]]. The season was their first since [[2013–14 FC Barcelona season|2013–14]] without [[Luis Suárez (Uruguayan footballer)|Luis Suárez]] and [[Ivan Rakitić]], who are respectively departed to [[Atlético Madrid]] and [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]].

Coming off a disastrous [[2019–20 FC Barcelona season|2019–20]] season, which not only ended trophyless for the first time in 12 years, but also produced a humiliating [[FC Barcelona 2–8 FC Bayern Munich|8–2 defeat]] to [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern München]] in the Champions League, Barcelona looked to bounce back. [[Ronald Koeman]] was brought in as manager in place of [[Quique Setién]], and he immediately emphasized his strive to reform the squad, underscored by the aforementioned departure of [[Luis Suárez (Uruguayan footballer)|Suárez]] to Atlético Madrid. This season saw Barça win a record-extending 31st Copa del Rey and fight until the end for the La Liga title, although several stumbles near the finish line meant they finished third, their lowest league position since [[2007–08 FC Barcelona season|2007–08]]. In the Champions League, Barcelona finished second in their group and then lost to [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|PSG]] in the round of 16, breaking their streak of 13 consecutive quarter-final appearances in the competition.

Although not known at the time, this season ended up being [[Lionel Messi]]'s last at Barcelona. He scored his last goal for the club in his last game, which Barça lost 1–2 to [[RC Celta de Vigo|Celta Vigo]] on 16 May 2021.

Barcelona utilized five sets of kits (excluding variations) throughout the season, a club record. This included a fourth [[Senyera]] stripe from the previous season and a 'special' ''Clásico'' kit which ended up being used against Real Madrid and Atlético Madrid in the second half of the season.

==Season overview==
===August===
On 17 August, [[Quique Setién]] was dismissed as the first team head coach after only seven months in charge.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1754842/quique-setien-no-longer-first-team-coach |title=Quique Setién no longer first team coach |date=17 August 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=22 August 2020}}</ref>

On 19 August, the club announced that [[Ronald Koeman]] would be the new head coach until 30 June 2022.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1755317/ronald-koeman-is-the-new-fc-barcelona-coach |title=Ronald Koeman is the new FC Barcelona coach |date=19 August 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=22 August 2020}}</ref>

===September===
On 1 September, Barcelona reached an agreement with [[Sevilla FC]] for the transfer of [[Ivan Rakitić]] for €1.5 million plus €9 million in variables.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1798820/agreement-with-sevilla-for-transfer-of-ivan-rakitic |title=Agreement with Sevilla for transfer of Ivan Rakitic |date=1 September 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=1 September 2020}}</ref>

On 21 September, Barcelona reached an agreement with [[PAOK FC]] for the transfer of [[Moussa Wagué]] on loan for the rest of the season without a buy option.<ref name="auto">{{cite news |title=Agreement with PAOK FC for the loan of Wague|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1837626/agreement-with-paok-fc-for-the-loan-of-wague|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=21 September 2020 |access-date=21 September 2020}}</ref>

On 22 September, Barcelona reached an agreement with [[Inter Milan]] for the [[Free transfer (association football)|free transfer]] of [[Arturo Vidal]] with €1 million in variables.<ref>{{cite news |title=Agreement with Inter Milan for the transfer of Arturo Vidal|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1837747/agreement-with-inter-milan-for-the-transfer-of-arturo-vidal|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=22 September 2020 |access-date=22 September 2020}}</ref>

On 23 September, Barcelona announced the transfer of [[Nélson Semedo]] to [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.]] for a fee of €30 million plus €10 million in variables.<ref>{{cite news |title=Agreement with Wolverhampton Wanderers for the transfer of Semedo|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1837922/agreement-with-wolverhampton-wanderers-for-the-transfer-of-semedo|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=23 September 2020 |access-date=23 September 2020}}</ref> On the same day, Barça announced that the club had reached an agreement with [[Atlético Madrid]] for the departure of [[Luis Suárez (Uruguayan footballer)|Luis Suárez]] on a free transfer with €6 million in variables.<ref>{{cite news |title=Agreement with Atlético Madrid for the transfer of Luis Suárez|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1837738/agreement-with-atletico-madrid-for-the-transfer-of-luis-suarez|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=23 September 2020 |access-date=24 September 2020}}</ref>

On 27 September, Barcelona won their [[La Liga]] opener in a 4–0 home win against [[Villarreal CF]]. A brace from [[Ansu Fati]], a [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty]] from [[Lionel Messi]], and an [[own goal]] from [[Pau Torres (footballer, born 1997)|Pau Torres]] gave Barça the victory.<ref>{{cite news |title=FC Barcelona v Villarreal: Four-midable (4-0)|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1845877/fc-barcelona-v-villarreal-four-midable-4-0|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=27 September 2020 |access-date=27 September 2020}}</ref>

===October===
On 1 October, Barcelona announced the signing of [[Sergiño Dest]] from [[AFC Ajax]] for a fee of €21 million plus €5 million in variables.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1849100/agreement-with-ajax-for-transfer-of-sergino-dest |title=Agreement with Ajax for transfer of Sergiño Dest |date=1 October 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=1 October 2020}}</ref> Later that same day, Barça defeated [[RC Celta de Vigo|Celta de Vigo]] 3–0 away from home. Another goal from Ansu Fati, a [[Lucas Olaza]] own goal, and a late goal from [[Sergi Roberto]] sealed the victory for the ''Blaugrana'', ending a five-year winless streak at the [[Balaídos]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1850061/rc-celta-0-3-fc-barcelona-looking-good |title=RC Celta 0-3 FC Barcelona: Looking good! |date=1 October 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=5 October 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://en.as.com/en/2020/10/01/football/1601574577_115439.html |title=Celta 0-3 Barcelona: 10-man Barça end Balaídos hoodoo |date=1 October 2020 |publisher=[[Diario AS]] |access-date=5 October 2020 |archive-date=4 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201004022606/https://en.as.com/en/2020/10/01/football/1601574577_115439.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On 4 October, Barcelona drew 1–1 with Sevilla at home. [[Luuk de Jong]] got the visitors off the mark but [[Philippe Coutinho]] equalized for the home side shortly after.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1856117/fc-barcelona-v-sevilla-all-square-1-1 |title=FC Barcelona v Sevilla: All square (1-1) |date=4 October 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=5 October 2020}}</ref>

On 5 October, Barcelona reached an agreement with [[S.L. Benfica]] for the loan of [[Jean-Clair Todibo]] with an option to buy for €20 million.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1856813/agreement-with-benfica-for-loan-of-todibo |title=Agreement with Benfica for loan of Todibo |date=5 October 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=5 October 2020}}</ref> The club also announced the departure of [[Rafinha (footballer, born February 1993)|Rafinha]] to [[Paris Saint-Germain]] on a free transfer.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1856896/agreement-with-psg-for-the-transfer-of-rafinha |title=Agreement with PSG for the transfer of Rafinha |date=5 October 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=5 October 2020}}</ref>

On 17 October, Barcelona lost 1–0 to [[Getafe CF]] away from home. [[Jaime Mata]] scored from the penalty spot to inflict Barça's first defeat of the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1866113/getafe-1-0-barca-first-league-defeat |title=Getafe 1-0 Barça: First league defeat |date=17 October 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=28 October 2020}}</ref>

On 20 October, Barcelona beat [[Ferencvárosi TC|Ferencváros]] 5–1 in their first [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] game of the [[2020–21 UEFA Champions League|season]]. Goals from Lionel Messi, Ansu Fati, Philippe Coutinho, [[Pedri]], and [[Ousmane Dembélé]] ensured victory for the ''Blaugrana''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/1870123/barca-5-1-ferencvaros-flying-start|title=Barça 5-1 Ferencváros: Flying start |date=20 October 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=28 October 2020}}</ref> Later that day, Barça announced the contract extensions of [[Gerard Piqué]] until 2024, [[Marc-André ter Stegen]] until 2025, [[Frenkie de Jong]] and [[Clément Lenglet]] until 2026.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/1870105/agreement-for-contract-extensions-for-pique-ter-stegen-de-jong-and-lenglet |title=Agreement for contract extensions for Piqué, Ter Stegen, De Jong and Lenglet |date=20 October 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=28 October 2020}}</ref>

On 24 October, Barcelona lost 3–1 at home to rivals [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in ''[[El Clásico]]''. [[Federico Valverde]] got the visitors off the mark early into the match but Ansu Fati equalized shortly after, in the process becoming the second youngest goalscorer in ''El Clásico'' history and scoring Barça's 400th goal in the fixture's history. [[Sergio Ramos]] scored from the penalty spot after a controversial penalty decision and [[Luka Modrić]] sealed the game off for ''Los Blancos''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1873978/barca-v-real-madrid-tough-defeat-to-take-1-3 |title=Barça v Real Madrid: Tough defeat to take (1-3) |date=24 October 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=28 October 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1873825/ansu-fati-scorer-of-barcas-400th-goal-against-real-madrid |title=Ansu Fati, scorer of Barça's 400th goal against Real Madrid |date=24 October 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=28 October 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://en.as.com/en/2020/10/24/football/1603551158_029898.html |title=Ansu Fati becomes second youngest scorer in El Clásico history |date=24 October 2020 |publisher=[[Diario AS]] |access-date=28 October 2020 |archive-date=30 November 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201130103114/https://en.as.com/en/2020/10/24/football/1603551158_029898.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On 27 October, President [[Josep Maria Bartomeu]] announced his resignation and the resignation of his board of directors, after six years of being the head of the club.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/club/news/1878687/josep-maria-bartomeu-announces-the-resignation-of-the-board-of-directors |title=Josep Maria Bartomeu announces the resignation of the Board of Directors |date=27 October 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=28 October 2020}}</ref>

On 28 October, Barcelona announced that Carles Tusquets would be the interim club president until elections were held. Later that same day, Barça defeated [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] 2–0 away from home in the Champions League. Goals from Dembélé and Messi gave Barça the victory.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/club/news/1878923/the-members-of-the-fc-barcelona-managing-committee |title=The members of the FC Barcelona Managing Committee |date=28 October 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=31 October 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/1879287/juventus-0-2-fc-barcelona-two-out-of-two|title=Juventus 0-2 FC Barcelona: Two out of two |date=28 October 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=29 October 2020}}</ref>

On 31 October, Barcelona drew 1–1 with [[Deportivo Alavés]]. [[Luis Rioja]] would take advantage of a mix-up between Gerard Piqué and [[Neto (footballer, born 1989)|Neto]] to put the home side 1–0 up. [[Antoine Griezmann]] would equalize in the second-half and score his first goal of the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1882758/alaves-1-1-barca-no-way-through|title=Alavés 1-1 Barça: No way through |date=31 October 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=31 October 2020}}</ref>

===November===
On 4 November, Barcelona defeated [[FC Dynamo Kyiv|Dynamo Kyiv]] 2–1 at home in the Champions League. An early goal from Messi and a [[Header (association football)|header]] from Piqué ensured victory for Barça.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/1887691/fc-barcelona-v-dynamo-kiev-100-record-in-europe-intact-2-1|title=FC Barcelona v Dynamo Kyiv: 100% record in Europe intact (2-1)|date=4 November 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=5 November 2020}}</ref>

On 7 November, Barcelona defeated [[Real Betis]] 5–2 at home. Goals from Dembélé, Griezmann, Pedri and a brace from Messi gave Barça the win.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/1891138/barca-5-2-betis-the-goals-are-back|title=Barça 5-2 Betis: The goals are back!|date=7 November 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=8 November 2020}}</ref>

On 21 November, Barcelona lost 1–0 to Atlético Madrid away from home. [[Yannick Carrasco]] scored the only goal after taking advantage of a mistake from Marc-André ter Stegen.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1902435/atletico-madrid-1-0-barca-first-defeat-at-wanda-metropolitano|title=Atlético Madrid 1-0 Barça: First defeat at Wanda Metropolitano|date=21 November 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=24 November 2020}}</ref>

On 24 November, Barcelona defeated Dynamo Kyiv 4–0 away from home in the Champions League. Sergiño Dest scored his first goal for Barcelona, [[Martin Braithwaite]] scored a brace, and Griezmann came off the bench to finish the game off.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1907798/dynamo-kyiv-0-4-fc-barcelona-into-the-last-sixteen|title=Dynamo Kyiv 0-4 FC Barcelona: Into the last sixteen!|date=24 November 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=25 November 2020}}</ref>

On 30 November, Barcelona defeated [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]] 4–0 at home. Braithwaite, Griezmann, Coutinho and Messi were the goalscorers.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/1919220/fc-barcelona-4-0-osasuna-anniversary-tribute-win|title=FC Barcelona 4-0 Osasuna: Anniversary tribute win|date=29 November 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=30 November 2020}}</ref>

===December===
On 2 December, Barcelona defeated Ferencváros 3–0 away from home in the Champions League. First half goals from Griezmann, Braithwaite and Dembélé were enough to secure a comfortable victory.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/1922930/ferencvros-0-3-fc-barcelona-100-per-cent|title=Ferencváros 0-3 FC Barcelona: 100 per cent record!|date=2 December 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=3 December 2020}}</ref>

On 5 December, Barcelona lost to [[Cádiz CF]] 2–1 away from home in the league. [[Álvaro Giménez]] scored first for the home side but Barça drew level with an own goal from [[Pedro Alcalá]]. The Andalusians went back in front after [[Álvaro Negredo]] came off the bench to score the winner.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1926462/cadiz-2-1-barca-no-joy-in-andalusia|title=Cádiz 2-1 Barça: No joy in Andalusia|date=5 December 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=6 December 2020}}</ref>

On 8 December, Barcelona lost to Juventus 3–0 at home in the Champions League after conceding two penalties converted by [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] and a goal from [[Weston McKennie]]. As a result, Barcelona finished 2nd in Champions League Group G.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1931231/fc-barcelona-0-3-juventus-not-our-night|title=FC Barcelona 0-3 Juventus: Not our night|date=8 December 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=11 December 2020}}</ref>

On 13 December, Barcelona defeated [[Levante UD|Levante]] 1–0 at home. Messi scored the only goal in the game.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1937977/fc-barcelona-1-0-levante-deserved-victory|title=FC Barcelona 1-0 Levante: Deserved victory|date=13 December 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=14 December 2020}}</ref>

On 16 December, Barcelona defeated [[Real Sociedad]] 2–1 at home.
[[Jordi Alba]] and Frenkie de Jong scored for Barça after trailing by one goal.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1943730/barca-2-1-real-sociedad-comeback-to-beat-the-leaders|title=Barça 2-1 Real Sociedad: Comeback to beat the leaders|date=16 December 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=17 December 2020}}</ref>

On 19 December, Barcelona drew 2–2 with [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] at home. Lionel Messi and [[Ronald Araújo]] were the goalscorers for Barça.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1946647/barca-2-2-valencia-points-shared-at-camp-nou|title=Barça 2-2 Valencia: Points shared at Camp Nou|date=19 December 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=20 December 2020}}</ref>

On 22 December, Barcelona defeated [[Real Valladolid]] 3–0 away from home. Lenglet, Braithwaite and Messi were the goalscorers. Messi surpassed [[Pelé]] as the highest goalscorer for a single club with his goal against Valladolid.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1950649/real-valladolid-0-3-fc-barcelona-pretty-in-pink|title=Real Valladolid 0-3 FC Barcelona: Pretty in pink|date=22 December 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=23 December 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1941432/leo-messi-surpasses-pele-as-highest-goalscorer-ever-for-a-single-club|title=Leo Messi surpasses Pelé as highest goalscorer ever for a single club|date= 23 December 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=23 December 2020}}</ref>

On 29 December, Barcelona drew 1–1 with [[SD Eibar|Eibar]] at home. [[Kike (footballer, born November 1989)|Kike]] got the visitors off the mark after taking advantage of an error by Araújo. Dembélé came off the bench to score the equalizer.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1959238/fc-barcelona-11-eibar-out-of-luck|title=FC Barcelona 1-1 Eibar: Out of luck|date=29 December 2020 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=30 December 2020}}</ref>

===January===
On 3 January, Barcelona defeated [[SD Huesca|Huesca]] 1–0 away from home. De Jong scored the only goal in the game.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/1965394/huesca-0-1-fc-barcelona-happy-new-year|title=Huesca 0-1 FC Barcelona: Happy New Year|date=3 January 2021 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=4 January 2021}}</ref>

On 6 January, Barcelona and Getafe reached an agreement for the loan of [[Carles Aleñá]] for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1966467/carles-alena-loaned-out-to-getafe|title=Carles Aleñá loaned out to Getafe|date=6 January 2021 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=7 January 2021}}</ref> Later that same day, Barcelona defeated [[Athletic Bilbao]] 3–2 away from home. [[Iñaki Williams]] gave an early lead for the home side but Pedri equalized with a header. Messi sealed victory for Barça by scoring two goals.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1967156/athletic-2-3-barca-three-glorious-points|title=Athletic 2-3 Barça: Three glorious points|date=6 January 2021 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=7 January 2021}}</ref>

On 9 January, Barcelona defeated [[Granada CF|Granada]] 4–0 away from home. Braces from Griezmann and Messi earned a comfortable victory for Barça.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/1969255/granada-0-4-barca-another-away-win|title=Granada 0-4 Barça: Another away win!|date=9 January 2021 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=10 January 2021}}</ref>

On 13 January, Barcelona defeated Real Sociedad in a [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]] 2–3 in the [[Supercopa de España]] after the score ended 1–1 during regulation time and [[Overtime (sports)|extra time]]. Frenkie de Jong put Barça in the lead after converting a header, but [[Mikel Oyarzabal]] equalized for ''La Real'' in the second half. Ter Stegen would go on to save two penalties in the shoot-out and [[Riqui Puig]] stepped up and scored the decisive penalty to send the Catalans to the final.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1973363/real-sociedad-1-1-barca-2-3-on-pens-ter-stegen-takes-us-to-seville|title=Real Sociedad 1-1 Barça (2-3 on pens): Ter Stegen takes us to Seville!|date=13 January 2021 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=14 January 2021}}</ref>

On 17 January, Barcelona lost 3–2 to Athletic Bilbao in the [[2021 Supercopa de España Final|Supercopa de España final]]. Antoine Griezmann struck first and put Barça in the lead but [[Óscar de Marcos]] quickly equalized. Griezmann would later score again, but [[Asier Villalibre]] scored in the final minute to make the score 2–2 and send the match into extra time. Iñaki Williams scored at the start of extra time and ''Los Leones'' won the Super Cup. The game also featured Lionel Messi's first red card while playing for FC Barcelona.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1977743/barca-2-3-athletic-club-painful-defeat|title=Barça 2-3 Athletic Club: Painful defeat|date=17 January 2021 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=19 January 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/barcelona/story/4291586/messi-could-face-4-match-ban-for-first-career-red-card-with-barcelona|title=Messi could face 4-match ban for first career red card with Barcelona|date=17 January 2021 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=22 January 2021}}</ref>

On 21 January, Barcelona defeated [[UE Cornellà|Cornellà]] 2–0 away from home in the [[Copa del Rey]]. Dembélé and Braithwaite scored the goals in extra time.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/1983185/cornella-0-2-fc-barcelona-victory-in-extra-time|title=Cornellà 0-2 FC Barcelona: Victory in extra time|date=21 January 2021 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=22 January 2021}}</ref>

On 24 January, Barcelona defeated [[Elche CF|Elche]] 2–0 at the [[Estadio Manuel Martínez Valero]]. Frenkie de Jong and Riqui Puig scored for the ''Blaugrana''. The latter also scored his first goal for the first team.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1984950/elche-2-0-barca-happy-away-days-continue|title=Elche 2-0 Barça: Happy away days continue|date=24 January 2021 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=24 January 2021}}</ref>

On 27 January, Barcelona defeated [[Rayo Vallecano]] 2–1 away from home in Copa del Rey round of 16. Rayo took the lead in the 63rd minute, but Barça came-back with goals from Messi and De Jong.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/1999876/rayo-vallecano-1-2-barca-safely-through-to-the-quarters|title=Rayo Vallecano 1-2 Barça: Safely through to the quarters|date=27 January 2021 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=30 January 2021}}</ref>

On 31 January, Barça defeated Athletic Bilbao 2–1 at home in La Liga. Messi scored his 650th for the club and Griezmann scored to claim all three points.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2006997/fc-barcelona-2-1-athletic-club-home-sweet-home|title=FC Barcelona 2-1 Athletic Club: Home sweet home|date=31 January 2021 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=31 January 2021}}</ref>

===February===
On 1 February, Barcelona announced that the club had reached an agreement with Benfica to terminate the loan of Jean-Clair Todibo. Todibo subsequently joined [[OGC Nice]] on loan until the remainder of the season, with an option to buy for €8.5 million.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2007367/agreement-with-ogc-nice-on-todibo-loan|title=Agreement with OGC Nice on Todibo loan|date=1 February 2021 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=1 February 2021}}</ref>

On 3 February, Barcelona defeated Granada 5–3 away from home in the Copa del Rey quarter-finals. The home side took a 2–0 lead through goals from [[Kenedy (footballer)|Kenedy]] and [[Roberto Soldado]], but Barça came back in the last minutes of the game with goals from Antoine Griezmann and Jordi Alba, forcing extra time. Barça took the lead in the 100th minute of extra time with a header from Griezmann, but Granada soon equalized with a penalty converted by [[Fede Vico]]. However, Barça again took the lead with a goal from De Jong, and the game was sealed with a rasping volley from Jordi Alba, assuring passage to the semi-finals.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2013902/granada-3-5-fc-barcelona-comeback-kings|title=Granada 3-5 FC Barcelona: Comeback Kings!|date=3 February 2021 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=6 February 2021}}</ref>

On 7 February, Barcelona defeated Real Betis 3–2 away from home. The hosts took the lead through [[Borja Iglesias]] but a goal from Messi and an own goal from [[Víctor Ruiz (footballer, born 1989)|Víctor Ruiz]] handed Barcelona the lead, until the latter made amends for his own goal by equalizing the game. [[Francisco Trincão]] came off the bench to score his first goal for Barça and secure the win.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/2020457/betis-2-3-barca-the-comeback-part-two|title=Betis 2-3 Barça: The Comeback, part two!|date=7 February 2021 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=9 February 2021}}</ref>

On 10 February, Barcelona lost to Sevilla 2–0 in the first leg of Copa del Rey semi-finals. [[Jules Koundé]] and former Barça player Ivan Rakitić scored the goals for Sevilla.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2023312/sevilla-2-0-barca-all-to-do-in-the-second-leg|title=Sevilla 2-0 Barça: All to do in the second leg|date=10 February 2021 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=10 February 2021}}</ref>

On 13 February, Barcelona defeated Deportivo Alavés 5–1 at home. Braces from Trincão and Messi and a goal from [[Junior Firpo]] led the ''Blaugrana'' to victory.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2027982/barca-5-1-alaves-fantasy-football|title=Barça 5-1 Alavés: Fantasy football|date=13 February 2021 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=13 February 2021}}</ref>

On 16 February, Barcelona lost to Paris Saint-Germain 4–1 at home in the first leg of the Champions League [[2020–21 UEFA Champions League knockout phase#Round of 16|round of 16]].
Messi scored from the penalty spot to put Barça in the lead but a hat-trick from [[Kylian Mbappé]] and a goal from [[Moise Kean]] gave the visitors the victory.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/2032021/fc-barcelona-1-4-paris-st-germain-painful-defeat|title=FC Barcelona 1-4 Paris St Germain: Painful defeat|date=16 February 2021 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=20 February 2021}}</ref>

On 21 February, Barcelona drew 1–1 with Cádiz at home. Messi scored from the penalty spot to give the lead for Barça but Cádiz drew late with a penalty converted by [[Álex Fernández (footballer, born 1992)|Álex Fernández]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/2038662/barca-1-1-cadiz-dominance-without-reward|title=Barça 1-1 Cádiz: Dominance without reward|date=21 February 2021 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=23 February 2021}}</ref>

On 24 February, Barcelona defeated Elche 3–0 at home. A brace from Messi and a goal from Jordi Alba were enough to take all three points.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2043290/fc-barcelona-3-0-elche-crucial-victory|title=FC Barcelona 3-0 Elche: Crucial victory|date=24 February 2021 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=24 February 2021}}</ref>

On 27 February, Barcelona defeated Sevilla 2–0 away from home. Dembélé and Messi were the goalscorers.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2045862/sevilla-0-2-barca-still-in-contention|title=Sevilla 0-2 Barça: Still in contention|date=27 February 2021 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=27 February 2021}}</ref>

===March===
On 3 March, Barcelona defeated Sevilla 3–0 (3–2 [[Playoff format#Total points series (aggregate)|agg.]]) in the second leg of Copa del Rey [[2020–21 Copa del Rey#Semi-finals|semi-finals]]. An early goal from Dembélé and a goal from Piqué in the last minute of the game leveled the aggregate score and forced the match into extra time. Martin Braithwaite scored the winning goal in 95th minute to secure a spot in the [[2021 Copa del Rey Final|final]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2052917/barca-3-0-sevilla-dramatic-victory-and-into-the-final|title=Barça 3-0 Sevilla: Dramatic victory and into the final!|date=3 March 2021 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=4 March 2021}}</ref>

On 6 March, Barcelona defeated Osasuna 2–0 away from home. Jordi Alba and [[Ilaix Moriba]] scored for the ''Blaugrana'', with the latter scoring his first senior goal.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/2057056/osasuna-0-2-fc-barcelona-another-happy-away-day|title=Osasuna 0-2 FC Barcelona: Another happy away day|date=6 March 2021 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=7 March 2021}}</ref>

On 7 March, [[Joan Laporta]] was [[2021 FC Barcelona presidential election|elected]] as the new club president, having previously served as club president from 2003 until 2010.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/club/news/2059811/joan-laporta-president-of-fc-barcelona|title=Joan Laporta, president of FC Barcelona|date=7 March 2021 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=8 March 2021}}</ref>

On 10 March, Barcelona drew 1–1 with Paris Saint-Germain in the second leg of the Champions League round of 16. Kylian Mbappé scored from the penalty spot to put Paris in the lead but Messi equalized for Barça shortly after. With an aggregate score of 5–2, Barcelona were eliminated from the Champions League.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2062799/psg-1-1-barca-pride-restored|title=PSG 1-1 Barça: Pride restored|date=10 March 2021 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=12 March 2021}}</ref>

On 15 March, Barcelona defeated Huesca 4–1 at home. A brace from Messi and goals from Griezmann and [[Óscar Mingueza]] – with his first senior goal – led the ''Blaugrana'' to victory.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2069522/barca-4-1-huesca-closer-to-the-top|title=Barça 4-1 Huesca: Closer to the top|date=15 March 2021 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=16 March 2021}}</ref>

On 21 March, Barcelona defeated Real Sociedad 6–1 away from home. Dest and Messi scored braces while Griezmann and Dembélé scored a goal each.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/2074922/real-sociedad-1-6-barca-six-of-the-best|title=Real Sociedad 1-6 Barça: Six of the best!|date=21 March 2021 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=22 March 2021}}</ref>

===April===
On 5 April, Barcelona defeated Real Valladolid 1–0 at home. Dembélé scored the winning goal in the 90th minute.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2095377/barca-1-0-valladolid-late-late-show-from-dembele|title=Barça 1-0 Valladolid: Late, late show from Dembélé!|date=5 April 2021 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=5 April 2021}}</ref> After this victory Barcelona stood one point away from Atlético, one week before El Clásico. This meant Barcelona had reduced the distance with La Liga's leaders by 11 points since last defeat against Cádiz on December 5, winning 51 of 57 possible points.

On 10 April, Barcelona lost 2–1 to fierce rivals Real Madrid away from home. First half goals came from [[Karim Benzema]] and [[Toni Kroos]], and while Óscar Mingueza pulled one back for the Catalans, however it wasn't enough as the visitors lost the first ''Clásico'' at the [[Alfredo Di Stéfano Stadium]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2100110/real-madrid-2-1-fc-barcelona-down-but-not-without-a-fight-at-valdebebas-2-1|title=Real Madrid 2-1 FC Barcelona: Down but not without a fight at Valdebebas (2-1)|date=10 April 2021 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=12 April 2021}}</ref>

On 17 April, Barcelona won their 31st Copa del Rey after defeating Athletic Bilbao 4–0 in the [[2021 Copa del Rey Final|final]]. De Jong and Griezmann scored a goal each while Messi scored a brace.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2108496/copa-del-rey-champions|title=Copa del Rey champions!|date=17 April 2021 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=17 April 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/2107669/fc-barcelona-win-their-31st-copa-del-rey-title|title=FC Barcelona win their 31st Copa del Rey title|date=17 April 2021 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=17 April 2021}}</ref>

On 22 April, Barcelona released a statement confirming that the Catalan club would be forming a part of a breakaway [[European Super League]], a proposed annual club football competition to be contested by twenty of [[Europe]]'s most elite football clubs. Later that day, Barça defeated Getafe 5–2 at home. A brace from Messi, a header from Araújo, a penalty converted by Griezmann and an own goal secured victory for the home side.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2115199/barca-5-2-getafe-still-in-the-hunt|title=Barça 5-2 Getafe: Still in the hunt!|date=22 April 2021 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=23 April 2021}}</ref>

On 25 April, Barcelona defeated Villarreal 2–1 away from home. A brace from Griezmann in the first half helped turn the tie around for the visitors after being a goal behind.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/news/2118748/villarreal-1-2-fc-barcelona-keeping-the-pressure-on|title=Villarreal 1-2 FC Barcelona: Keeping the pressure on|date=25 April 2021 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=26 April 2021}}</ref>

On 29 April, Barcelona lost 2–1 to Granada at home. Messi gave Barcelona the lead in the first half, but the ''Blaugrana'' ended up being the losing side after conceding two goals in the second half from [[Darwin Machís]] and [[Jorge Molina (footballer, born 1982)|Jorge Molina]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2122678/barca-1-2-granada-opportunity-missed|title=Barça 1-2 Granada: Opportunity missed|date=29 April 2021 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=29 April 2021}}</ref>

===May===
On 2 May, Barcelona defeated Valencia 3–2 away from home. A brace from Messi and a goal scored by Griezmann secured  victory for the visitors after being a goal behind.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2127597/valencia-2-3-barca-on-fire-at-mestalla|title=Valencia 2-3 Barça: On fire at Mestalla!|date=2 May 2021 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=2 May 2021}}</ref>

On 8 May, Barcelona drew 0–0 against Atlético Madrid at home.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2132923/fc-barcelona-0-0-atletico-madrid-missed-opportunity|title=FC Barcelona 0-0 Atlético Madrid: Missed opportunity|date=8 May 2021 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=8 May 2021}}</ref>

On 11 May, Barcelona drew 3–3 against Levante away from home. Goals from Messi and Pedri gave Barça a two-goal lead in the first half, but Levante equalized after scoring two goals in two minutes. Barcelona restored the lead with a goal from Dembélé, but the lead was cancelled out again after the home side scored a goal.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2138978/levante-3-3-barca-title-challenge-takes-a-blow|title=Levante 3-3 Barça: Title challenge takes a blow|date=11 May 2021 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=12 May 2021}}</ref>

On 16 May, Barcelona lost 2–1 to Celta Vigo at home. Messi gave Barcelona the lead, but a brace from [[Santi Mina]] won the game for Celta.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2145750/barca-1-2-celta-title-hopes-over|title=Barça 1-2 Celta: Title hopes over|date=16 May 2021 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=17 May 2021}}</ref>

On 22 May, Barcelona defeated Eibar 1–0 away from home, with Griezmann scoring the only goal of the game. Barcelona ended the season with a third place finish in La Liga, its lowest since [[2007–08 La Liga|2007–08]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2153616/eibar-01-fc-barcelona-griezmann-helps-barca-to-round-off-season-with-a-win|title=Eibar 0–1 FC Barcelona: Griezmann helps Barça to round off season with a win|date=22 May 2021 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=22 May 2021}}</ref>
